newsitem.title: USA: United HealthCare sees enrollment gains.
newsitem.headline: United HealthCare sees enrollment gains.

text.p: United HealthCare Corp sees health plan enrollment gains of 15 to 20 percent in 1997, with growth in both commercial and government segments, said Chief Executive Dr William McGuire at a Smith Barney Health Care Services conference in New York.

He said that medical costs trends should stabilize at three to four percent in 1997, similar to the rate in 1996. He said the consumer-driven utilization will have upward pressure on costs trends, but that the company would try to offset these by managing key cost escalators.

He also said that United should see lower selling general and administrative (SGNA) spending in 1997 because of improved efficiency. In the third quarter of '96 SGNA spending was 21.2 percent of total revenues down from 21.7 percent in the second quarter but up from the 14.4 percent year-ago figure.
Premiums in commercial health plan of five percent or more could be expected for the coming year, McGuire said.
He said the company has started a new initiative of rural health and expected to start up in 15 states initially.

He said the uncertain areas for 1997 would be seasonally in medical costs, such as a influenza outbreak, unit costs changes in areas of provider consolidation, consumer and payer benefit demands, and utilization of services and goods that "may be difficult to manage prospectively."
On the political and regulatory funds, he said the company was protecting itself by not being too heavily exposed in any one area.
The company expects to release fourth quarter and year end results this Thursday.
